title: Marathon Preorders Included A Forced Destiny 2 Download, But It's Fixed Now
description: Preorders for Bungie's new shooter Marathon went live this week, but things did not go entirely to plan for the PC version on Steam. People reported that upon preordering Marathon on Steam, they also got Destiny 2 automatically installed without any prompting. This was an issue that Bungie has now fixed, the developer said. Additionally, Bungie said it fixed an issue with the Collector's Edition that caused players to get an error when trying to activate game codes on Steam. People who buy Marathon before release get free cosmetics for Destiny 2, and some theorized this could be related to the issue. However, Bungie did not explain why or how these issues occurred. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Peak's Final Biome Will Replace Caldera, But Not Soon
description: Peak will get a new biome in 2026, according to co-developer Aggro Crab. The new segment of the climb will replace the game’s existing Caldera area, though players shouldn’t expect it anytime soon. The biome is planned as a later update and is still early enough that the studio isn’t ready to share specifics about what it will look like or how it will play. The Caldera replacement is part of a broader plan to slow Peak’s update cadence in 2026. Aggro Crab confirmed that there are still a couple of updates in development that focus on commonly requested features from players, but those updates will roll out less frequently than in the past. The studio declined to detail what those features are, saying it wants to talk about them closer to release. Once those updates are finished, Aggro Crab and co-developer Landfall plan to begin work on Peak’s final biome. That biome will swap places with Caldera, marking the last major environment change planned for the game. While the studio said it’s excited about the idea, it emphasized that this is meant to be a longer-term goal rather than something arriving in the near future. Continue Reading at GameSpot

description: The early access launch of Hytale has been a huge success, with over a million players hopping in and exploring the new sandbox title. However, you can bring the experience of a console to Hytale if you don't want to use a mouse and keyboard when playing on PC. title: The Prince Of Persia Series Will Continue Despite The Sands Of Time Remake Cancellation
description: After a prolonged development period, Ubisoft hit the brakes on the remake of Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time. But in the wake of the disappointing news, the publisher said that it isn't calling it quits on the long-running franchise. The remake was canceled as the project wasn't able to "reach the level of quality" expected from fans, according to a statement from the Prince of Persia development team on X. The statement added that the team didn't want to "release something short of what The Sands of Time represents." The statement goes on to read: "Prince of Persia as a universe and a legacy continues to matter deeply to us, and this decision does not mean we're stepping away from the franchise." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: New York Times Releases Its First Multiplayer Word Game, Crossplay
description: The New York Times' games are filled with single-player experiences, but now the news organization is launching its first two-player game as a standalone app. Starting today, NYT is inviting readers to try Crossplay, a game that should seem very familiar to anyone who has tried Words with Friends or Scrabble. Crossplay is now live, and this is how it works: Players start each game with seven letters on the same board. The object is to score points from creating words or playing off of the words that are already on the board. More points are awarded depending upon the rarity of the letter and where it's placed on a the board. Each player has a limited number of tile bags that are lost after a tile is played on the board. Once players run out of tiles, Crossplay enters one final round to give both players one last chance to succeed. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Battlefield 6 Community Update Reveals Season 2 Plans And Testing For Solo BR
description: The latest Battlefield 6 community update details some of the new content planned for Season 2, including a brand-new multiplayer map called Contaminated. The developer also teased the return of a classic Battlefield 4 map, and it gave an update on the likelihood of a solo playlist for Redsec battle royale. As previously announced, Battlefield 6's Season 2 update has been delayed, and Battlefield Studios is currently using the extra time to develop and refine the upcoming seasonal content. The new community update reveals Battlefield Labs is being used to test on one of Season 2's new maps called Contaminated. The studio says it is using the map to evaluate how vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, alongside cover and asset placement, and objective boundaries. Season 2's Containment mapThe developer says the full map reveal for Contaminated will arrive at a later date, but it did provide an image on social media for the first official look of the map, as seen in the image above. The studio also confirms that the map's size falls somewhere between Eastwood and Mirak Valley. It is also comparable to classic Battlefield maps such as St. Quentin Scar from Battlefield 1 or Arras from Battlefield 5. Contaminated will also have unique gameplay mechanics, and these will be tested in live matches within Battlefield Labs. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Highguard, The Confusing TGA Closer, Shows Life Ahead Of Launch Next Week
description: If you tuned into Geoff Keighley's TGA ceremony in December last year, you might recall how odd it seemed to have the show end with Highguard, a new free-to-play, hero-based shooter from former Titanfall 2 and Apex Legends developers. What you might not remember is that Highguard is out in just a couple of days, with not much to show for it. That might have initially indicated that the shooter was primed for a delay, but subtle changes to the game's listing on Steam paint a different picture. Updates to the listing have been occurring since the game's reveal, but a few over the past two days certainly make it seem like Highguard has no intention to miss its January 26 release date. In just the last 24 hours, developer Wildlight Entertainment has made changes to the listing's various tags and made several package changes in the background, with similar activity happening the day before, too. That isn't to say the Steam listing is any more fleshed out. Right now if you navigate to Highguard on Steam, you'll see the game's release date and a very short blurb describing its blend of hero shooting and PvP raiding gameplay, along with the game's debut trailer and associated screenshots. It's sparse for a game that is less than a week from release, and no different to what was available when it was first revealed last month. Continue Reading at GameSpot
